title: "Morning Board"

```{python}
# | tags: [setup]
import json
from pathlib import Path

import pandas as pd
import plotly.graph_objects as go
from IPython.display import HTML, Markdown, display

DATA = Path("data")
px_all = pd.read_csv(DATA / "prices.csv", parse_dates=["date"])
meta = json.loads((DATA / "meta.json").read_text(encoding="utf-8"))

# Last bar per ticker, plus the bar before it (for the 1-day change) and the
# bar 5 sessions back (for the week change).
px_all = px_all.sort_values(["ticker", "date"])
g = px_all.groupby("ticker")
last = g.tail(1).set_index("ticker")
def nth_back(n: int) -> pd.Series:
    """Close n sessions before the last bar, per ticker (NA if not enough history)."""
    return g["close"].apply(lambda s: s.iloc[-1 - n] if len(s) > n else pd.NA)


prev_close, week_close, month_close = nth_back(1), nth_back(5), nth_back(21)

last["chg_1d"] = (last["close"] / prev_close - 1) * 100
last["chg_1w"] = (last["close"] / week_close - 1) * 100
last["chg_1m"] = (last["close"] / month_close - 1) * 100


def series(ticker: str) -> pd.DataFrame:
    return px_all[px_all["ticker"] == ticker]


def signed(x, dp=2, suffix="%"):
    if pd.isna(x):
        return '<span class="stamp">—</span>'
    cls = "up" if x >= 0 else "down"
    return f'<span class="{cls}">{x:+.{dp}f}{suffix}</span>'
```

Markdown(f"<p class='stamp'>Last bar **{meta['last_bar']}** · fetched {meta['fetched_at_utc']} · "
         f"{meta['ok']}/{meta['requested']} tickers</p>")

## Market

```{python}
STRIP = [("SPY", "S&P 500"), ("QQQ", "Nasdaq 100"), ("^VIX", "VIX"),
         ("^VIX3M", "VIX3M"), ("^TNX", "10Y yield"), ("DX-Y.NYB", "Dollar")]

cards = []
for sym, label in STRIP:
    if sym not in last.index:
        continue
    row = last.loc[sym]
    cards.append(
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">{label}</div>'
        f'<div class="value">{row["close"]:,.2f}</div>'
        f'<div class="delta">{signed(row["chg_1d"])}</div></div>'
    )

# Volatility stress: VIX3M/VIX below 1 means front-month fear — worth its own tile.
if {"^VIX", "^VIX3M"} <= set(last.index):
    ratio = last.loc["^VIX3M", "close"] / last.loc["^VIX", "close"]
    state = "stressed" if ratio < 1 else "calm"
    cls = "down" if ratio < 1 else "up"
    cards.append(
        f'<div class="stat"><div class="label">VIX3M / VIX</div>'
        f'<div class="value">{ratio:.2f}</div>'
        f'<div class="delta {cls}">{state}</div></div>'
    )

HTML(f'<div class="stat-strip">{"".join(cards)}</div>')
```

### SPY

```{python}
# Daily / Weekly / Monthly candles. The site is static, so all three timeframes
# are computed here and shipped in the figure; Plotly's own buttons swap which
# set is visible. No custom JS, and it works offline.
TIMEFRAMES = [("Daily", None, 130), ("Weekly", "W-FRI", 104), ("Monthly", "ME", 60)]
MA_SPEC = [("sma10", "#3498db", 1.0), ("sma20", "#e67e22", 1.0), ("sma50", "#9b59b6", 1.4)]
WEEKEND_BREAK = [dict(bounds=["sat", "mon"])]


def timeframe_frame(df: pd.DataFrame, rule: str | None, bars: int) -> pd.DataFrame:
    """OHLC at the requested timeframe, with MAs recomputed on that timeframe.

    A 10-period MA means 10 *weeks* on the weekly chart — resampling the daily
    MA instead would just be a sampled daily line wearing a weekly label.
    """
    if rule is None:
        out = df.copy()  # daily: MAs already computed by lib.fetch
    else:
        out = (df.set_index("date")
                 .resample(rule)
                 .agg({"open": "first", "high": "max", "low": "min",
                       "close": "last", "volume": "sum"})
                 .dropna(subset=["close"])
                 .reset_index())
        for col, _, _ in MA_SPEC:
            out[col] = out["close"].rolling(int(col.removeprefix("sma"))).mean()
    return out.tail(bars)


def candle_figure(df: pd.DataFrame, name: str, height: int = 400) -> go.Figure:
    frames = [(label, timeframe_frame(df, rule, bars)) for label, rule, bars in TIMEFRAMES]
    per_tf = 1 + len(MA_SPEC)

    fig = go.Figure()
    for i, (_, f) in enumerate(frames):
        vis = i == 0
        fig.add_trace(go.Candlestick(
            x=f["date"], open=f["open"], high=f["high"], low=f["low"], close=f["close"],
            increasing_line_color="#18bc9c", decreasing_line_color="#e74c3c",
            name=name, visible=vis, showlegend=False))
        for col, color, width in MA_SPEC:
            fig.add_trace(go.Scatter(
                x=f["date"], y=f[col], mode="lines", name=col.upper(),
                line=dict(color=color, width=width), visible=vis))

    fig.update_layout(
        height=height,
        margin=dict(l=8, r=8, t=34, b=26),
        template="plotly_white",
        xaxis_rangeslider_visible=False,
        xaxis=dict(rangebreaks=WEEKEND_BREAK),
        yaxis=dict(side="right", tickformat=",.0f"),
        legend=dict(orientation="h", y=1.0, yanchor="bottom", x=0, xanchor="left",
                    font=dict(size=11)),
    )
    return fig


def timeframe_switch(host_id: str) -> str:
    """Button group + the script that swaps timeframes on the adjacent chart.

    Plotly's own `updatemenus` buttons are locked to ~33px tall regardless of
    font or padding, which is under the touch-target guideline, and they eat
    chart height by living inside the plot. Real buttons cost ~15 lines of JS
    and behave properly on a phone.
    """
    per_tf = 1 + len(MA_SPEC)
    n = len(TIMEFRAMES) * per_tf
    states = []
    for i, (label, _, _) in enumerate(TIMEFRAMES):
        visible = [False] * n
        for j in range(per_tf):
            visible[i * per_tf + j] = True
        # Weekend gaps only exist on the daily axis; keeping the rangebreak on a
        # weekly/monthly chart would blank out most of the candles.
        states.append({"visible": visible,
                       "rangebreaks": WEEKEND_BREAK if i == 0 else []})

    btns = "".join(
        f'<button type="button" data-tf="{i}"'
        f'{" class=\"active\"" if i == 0 else ""}>{label}</button>'
        for i, (label, _, _) in enumerate(TIMEFRAMES))

    return f"""
<div class="tf-switch" id="{host_id}" role="group" aria-label="Candle timeframe">{btns}</div>
<script>
(function () {{
  var STATES = {json.dumps(states)};
  var host = document.getElementById({host_id!r});
  function chart() {{
    // The chart Quarto renders immediately after this button group.
    var el = host.parentElement.querySelector('.plotly-graph-div');
    return el || document.querySelector('.plotly-graph-div');
  }}
  function attach() {{
    var gd = chart();
    if (!gd || typeof Plotly === 'undefined') return setTimeout(attach, 60);
    host.addEventListener('click', function (ev) {{
      var b = ev.target.closest('button[data-tf]');
      if (!b) return;
      var s = STATES[+b.dataset.tf];
      Plotly.update(gd, {{visible: s.visible}}, {{'xaxis.rangebreaks': s.rangebreaks}});
      host.querySelectorAll('button').forEach(function (x) {{ x.classList.remove('active'); }});
      b.classList.add('active');
    }});
  }}
  attach();
}})();
</script>
"""


display(HTML(timeframe_switch("tf-spy")))
candle_figure(series("SPY"), "SPY").show(
    config={"responsive": True, "displayModeBar": False})
```

## Watchlist

```{python}
COLS = [
    ("close", "Close", "{:,.2f}"),
    ("chg_1d", "1D", None),
    ("chg_1w", "1W", None),
    ("chg_1m", "1M", None),
    ("rsi", "RSI", "{:.0f}"),
    ("sma50_atr_ext", "ATR ext", "{:+.1f}"),
    ("pct_ema8", "vs 8EMA", None),
    ("adr", "ADR", None),
    ("rel_vol", "Rel vol", "{:.2f}"),
]

wl = last[last["group"] == "watchlist"].sort_values("chg_1d", ascending=False)

head = "".join(f"<th>{label}</th>" for _, label, _ in COLS)
rows = []
for tkr, row in wl.iterrows():
    cells = []
    for col, _, fmt in COLS:
        val = row[col]
        if col == "adr":
            cells.append(f"<td>{val * 100:.1f}%</td>" if pd.notna(val) else "<td>—</td>")
        elif fmt is None:
            cells.append(f"<td>{signed(val)}</td>")
        elif pd.isna(val):
            cells.append("<td>—</td>")
        else:
            cells.append(f"<td>{fmt.format(val)}</td>")
    # Trend flags: above both the 10 and 20 SMA is the simple "in gear" read.
    gear = "▲" if row["close"] > row["sma20"] and row["close"] > row["sma10"] else ""
    rows.append(f"<tr><td>{tkr} <span class='up'>{gear}</span></td>{''.join(cells)}</tr>")

HTML(f"<div class='table-wrap'><table class='board'><thead><tr><th>Ticker</th>{head}</tr>"
     f"</thead><tbody>{''.join(rows)}</tbody></table></div>")
```

::: {.stamp}
ATR ext = distance from the 50-day SMA measured in ATRs. ADR = average daily
range as a % of close. Rel vol = volume vs its own 20-day average.
:::
